text: A unital left R-module is an abelian group M acted on by a ring R with identity, satisfying r(m+n)=rm+rn, (r+s)m=rm+sm, (rs)m=r(sm), and 1m=m. The ring need not be commutative.
provenance: Original formulation of the module axioms, checked directly; Stacks Project commutative-ring conventions provide context: https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00AQ. No source prose reproduced.

text: For left modules M,N over a commutative ring R with identity, the canonical map M x N -> M tensor_R N is R-bilinear. Every R-bilinear map M x N -> P factors uniquely through an R-linear map M tensor_R N -> P.
provenance: Original formulation checked against the tensor-product universal property in Stacks Project: https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00CV. No source prose reproduced.

text: For modules M,N over a commutative ring R with identity, M tensor_R N is the free R-module on symbols [m,n], modulo additivity in both entries and [rm,n]=r[m,n]=[m,rn]. The class of [m,n] is written m tensor n.
provenance: Original formulation checked against the tensor-product construction in Stacks Project: https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00CV. No source prose reproduced.

text: Every abelian group A has a unique unital Z-module structure: positive integers act by repeated addition, 0 acts as zero, and (-n)a=-(na). For example, Z/8Z is generated by [1], with 8[1]=0.
provenance: Original example verified from module axioms and modular arithmetic; module context checked at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00AR. No source prose reproduced.

text: The subset 3Z x 2Z is a Z-submodule of Z^2. Its quotient Z^2/(3Z x 2Z) is isomorphic to Z/3Z x Z/2Z, via (a,b) -> ([a] mod 3,[b] mod 2).
provenance: Original example checked by the displayed surjective homomorphism and its kernel; quotient-module context checked at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00AR. No source prose reproduced.

text: For an R-module element m, Ann_R(m)={r in R : rm=0}. In the Z-module Z/12Z, Ann_Z([8])=3Z because 12 divides 8r exactly when 3 divides r.
provenance: Original formulation and arithmetic example; annihilator definition checked at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00AR. No source prose reproduced.

text: If M=Rm is a cyclic module over a commutative ring R with identity, the surjection R -> M, r -> rm, has kernel Ann_R(m). Thus M is isomorphic to R/Ann_R(m); in Z/12Z the submodule generated by [8] is isomorphic to Z/3Z.
provenance: Original formulation verified by the displayed map and its kernel, with direct arithmetic example; context checked at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00AR. No source prose reproduced.

text: The free left R-module R^3 has basis e1,e2,e3: each element is uniquely r1e1+r2e2+r3e3. An R-linear map R^3 -> M is uniquely specified by the three images of these basis vectors.
provenance: Original example verified from coordinatewise operations and the basis definition; free-module context checked at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00AR. No source prose reproduced.

text: For a module M over a commutative ring R with identity, R tensor_R M is isomorphic to M by r tensor m -> rm. Its inverse sends m to 1 tensor m.
provenance: Original formulation checked against Stacks Project Lemma 10.12.3: https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00CY. No source prose reproduced.

text: Over a commutative ring R with identity, (M direct-sum N) tensor_R P is isomorphic to (M tensor_R P) direct-sum (N tensor_R P), sending (m,n) tensor p to (m tensor p,n tensor p).
provenance: Original formulation checked against Stacks Project Lemma 10.12.3: https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00CY. No source prose reproduced.

text: For a commutative ring R with identity, R^2 tensor_R R^3 has a basis of six elements ei tensor fj, for 1<=i<=2 and 1<=j<=3. The coordinates of (a,b) tensor (c,d,e) are (ac,ad,ae,bc,bd,be).
provenance: Original finite-free example derived from tensoring direct sums and the tensor unit, checked against https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00CY. No source prose reproduced.

text: For an ideal I of a commutative ring R with identity and an R-module M, (R/I) tensor_R M is isomorphic to M/IM, with (r+I) tensor m mapped to rm+IM. In particular, (Z/5Z) tensor_Z Z^2 is isomorphic to (Z/5Z)^2.
provenance: Original formulation derived by tensoring I -> R -> R/I -> 0 and identifying its image IM; right exactness checked against https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00DF. No source prose reproduced.

text: For positive integers a,b, (Z/aZ) tensor_Z (Z/bZ) is isomorphic to Z/gcd(a,b)Z. Thus (Z/12Z) tensor_Z (Z/18Z) is Z/6Z, while (Z/4Z) tensor_Z (Z/9Z) is the zero module.
provenance: Original examples calculated as (Z/bZ)/a(Z/bZ), using tensor right exactness checked at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00DF. No source prose reproduced.

text: For modules M,N,P over a commutative ring R with identity, Hom_R(M tensor_R N,P) is isomorphic to Hom_R(M,Hom_R(N,P)). A map f corresponds to m -> (n -> f(m tensor n)).
provenance: Original formulation checked against Stacks Project Lemma 10.12.8: https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00DE. No source prose reproduced.

text: For a commutative ring R with identity, a multiplicative subset S containing 1, and an R-module M, S^(-1)R tensor_R M is isomorphic to S^(-1)M by (a/s) tensor m -> am/s. For R=Z and M=Z/6Z, inverting 2 leaves a module isomorphic as an abelian group to Z/3Z.
provenance: Original formulation: localization-tensor isomorphism checked at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00DK. Original example verified by making multiplication by 2 invertible and killing the 2-primary summand. No source prose reproduced.

text: The injective Z-module map Z -> Z, n -> 2n, becomes the zero map Z/2Z -> Z/2Z after tensoring with Z/2Z. Tensor products preserve right exactness, but need not preserve injectivity.
provenance: Original formulation checked against Stacks Project Example 10.12.12 and Lemma 10.12.10: https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00DI and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00DF. No source prose reproduced.
